---
title: "Factors with forcats"
subtitle: "Create, reorder, recode, and combine categorical variables"
---

R represents categorical data with **factors**. A factor is an integer
vector with a `levels` attribute that maps integers to categorical values —
when you view a factor, R displays the levels, not the underlying integers.
The forcats package provides tools for working with them.

::: {.source-note}
📄 Based on the Factors cheatsheet · forcats 1.0.1
:::

## Creating and inspecting factors

::: {.fn-ref}
`factor(x, levels, labels = levels, ordered = FALSE)`
: Convert a vector to a factor. Also `as_factor()`. `f <- factor(c("a","c","b","a"), levels = c("a","b","c"))`

`levels(x)`
: Return or set the levels of a factor. `levels(f); levels(f) <- c("x","y","z")`
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Use `unclass()` on a factor to see its underlying integer/levels structure.
:::

### Inspect factors

::: {.fn-ref}
`fct_count(f, sort = FALSE, prop = FALSE)`
: Count the number of values with each level.

`fct_match(f, lvls)`
: Check whether given levels are present in `f`.

`fct_unique(f)`
: Return the unique values, removing duplicates.
:::

## Change the order of levels

::: {.fn-ref}
`fct_relevel(.f, ..., after = 0L)`
: Manually reorder factor levels. `fct_relevel(f, c("b", "c", "a"))`

`fct_infreq(f)`
: Reorder levels by frequency of appearance, highest first. Also `fct_inseq()`.

`fct_inorder(f)`
: Reorder levels by the order in which they first appear in the data.

`fct_rev(f)`
: Reverse level order.

`fct_shift(f)`
: Shift levels left or right, wrapping around the end.

`fct_shuffle(f)`
: Randomly permute the order of factor levels.

`fct_reorder(.f, .x, .fun = median)`
: Reorder levels by their relationship with another variable — great for ordered bar/box plots. `boxplot(weight ~ fct_reorder(group, weight), data = PlantGrowth)`

`fct_reorder2(.f, .x, .y, .fun = last2)`
: Reorder levels by their final values when plotted against two other variables — handy for coloring line plots so the legend order matches the lines.
:::

## Change the value of levels

::: {.fn-ref}
`fct_recode(.f, ...)`
: Manually rename levels. Also `fct_relabel()`, which applies a function (purrr-style) to each level. `fct_recode(f, v = "a", x = "b", z = "c")`

`fct_anon(f, prefix = "")`
: Anonymize levels by replacing them with random integers.

`fct_collapse(.f, ..., other_level = NULL)`
: Collapse levels into manually defined groups. `fct_collapse(f, x = c("a", "b"))`

`fct_lump_min(f, min)`
: Lump together levels that appear fewer than `min` times into "Other". Also `fct_lump_n()`, `fct_lump_prop()`, `fct_lump_lowfreq()`.

`fct_other(f, keep, drop, other_level = "Other")`
: Replace levels not in `keep` (or in `drop`) with "Other".
:::

## Add or drop levels

::: {.fn-ref}
`fct_drop(f, only)`
: Drop unused levels.

`fct_expand(f, ...)`
: Add new levels to a factor. `fct_expand(f, "x")`

`fct_na_value_to_level(f, level = "(Missing)")`
: Assign an explicit level to `NA`s so they show up in plots and tables.
:::

## Combine factors

::: {.fn-ref}
`fct_c(...)`
: Combine factors that have different levels. Also `fct_cross()`. `fct_c(f1, f2)`

`fct_unify(fs, levels = lvls_union(fs))`
: Standardize levels across a list of factors so they can be safely combined or compared.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
A quick mental model: creating and reordering levels changes how a factor
*displays* and *sorts* (great for plots and tables); recoding, collapsing,
and lumping change what the levels actually *mean*.
:::
